source_snapshot.items: Test connections between BMC I2C-6 and UPHY1 from second PG548
source_snapshot.procedure: On BMC reads bus5 mux0x75, writes0x04 for port2 and refers to PID1114953.
source_snapshot.criteria: No expected downstream reply, mux readback, timeout, isolation or restoration state.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; replaces the remote functional transaction with unsupported physical probing/soldering.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Adds mux safety but incorrectly makes physical/manual evidence decisive.

old_problem: BMC I2C-6-to-bus5 mapping, second-PG548 mux0x75 port2/downstream topology, expected replies, exclusive raw access, combined-bit policy, sibling-path isolation and exact restoration are missing; prior reviews invent physical-only coverage.
disposition_reason: The source is a BMC-side functional test, not inherently Manual Only, but ED-03 prohibits guessing OEM controller/mux/downstream data. It remains Pending/Requires Confirmation until PID1114953 and safe reversible access define measurable acceptance.
decision_basis: Read row124/history2515 and kept second-PG548 mux0x75 independent from first-PG548 mux0x71 row123 and UPHY0 row125.
Preserved BMC login, bus5, mux0x75,0x04, port2, second PG548, UPHY1 and PID1114953.
Rejected mandatory probing/solder/photos not present in the protected procedure.
Required downstream response matrix, sibling-path isolation, bus ownership and exact original-byte restoration.
No scan, forced read/write, mux routing change, BMC reset, probe or DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: Second PG548 BMC I2C-6 to UPHY1 functional path
test_case.purpose: Verify the distinct second-PG548 route from logical BMC I2C-6 through bus5 mux0x75 port2 to PID-defined UPHY1 endpoints, without disturbing first-PG548/other channels, then restore the exact prior mux state.
required_package: PID1114953 second-PG548 mux0x75 port2 topology and downstream response matrix
Proof BMC I2C-6 maps to i2c-tools bus5
Downstream transactions, timeouts/NACK rules, sibling isolation, original-state restore and BMC recovery
test_case.test_command: After approval, capture BMC health, ownership and the original0x75 byte; select port2 using the approved0x04 or masked equivalent; verify readback; issue only PID-defined bounded UPHY1 reads; check that first-PG548 and other channels remain healthy; restore the exact original byte and revalidate services.
test_case.expected_result: The signed second-PG548 downstream endpoints return expected replies within bounds through mux0x75 port2, sibling/management paths show no impact, and mux/readback plus every relevant endpoint/service return exactly to baseline.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires proven controller/path identity, approved select semantics, downstream replies, isolation and exact restoration. A mux ACK alone, blind scan, NACK/timeout/arbitration loss, sibling impact, wrong readback or incomplete restore fails; physical photos are not required absent separate approval.
safety_gate: Authoritative BMC/platform topology and independent management recovery.
No raw/force access while mux0x75/bus5 is owned or busy.
Capture original byte; preserve required bits and sibling routes.
One bounded select/read sequence; abort and restore on any bus/service degradation.
expected_evidence: BMC/i2c-tools identity, owner/concurrency and management baseline
Original mux byte, select transcript and readback interpretation
Exact restoration/readback, endpoint/service health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Restore the exact recorded mux byte through the approved BMC path, confirm first/second PG548 isolation, all listed endpoints and management services. Use independent BMC recovery only for a stuck bus; do not scan or reset automatically.

source_conflict.reason: Criteria lacks a measurable reply and bus mapping; prior AI reviews add unsupported physical-only requirements.

blocked.reason: The functional target and commands are identifiable; PID map, oracle, exclusivity and restoration are resolvable execution gates.
